articles.title: Nepal government building falls into a river amid heavy flooding
articles.summary: The municipality building in Baglung was left teetering on an unstable ledge due to floods before it fell into a river.
articles.body:
Massive flooding left a government building in western Nepal teetering on the edge of an unstable ledge before it fell into the Daram River.

Witnesses captured the moment that the building in Baglung collapsed on Sunday, 27 September.

Officials removed important documents and computers from the building before it fell, local ward chair Tej Thapa confirmed to the BBC. No one was injured.

Landslides and floods have killed at least 27 people over recent days, according to Nepal's national disaster agency, only weeks after a flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border killed 1,400 people and left thousands more missing.

articles.title: Delhi records coolest September morning for second time
articles.summary: Delhi saw its second coolest September morning at 21°C; Ridge hit 16.9°C. September rainfall was 79.7 mm, a 35.5% deficit, IMD said.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The city experienced its coolest morning for the second time this month, with the minimum temperature dropping to 21 degrees Celsius, two notches below normal, at its base station Safdarjung Tuesday.Ridge observatory in north Delhi was cooler, recording Delhi’s lowest minimum at 16.9°C, six notches below normal.The mercury in Safdarjung had dropped to 21°C Sunday as well, making it the lowest minimum temperature recorded in Sept in the city in the past 18 years and the second lowest since 2001. “The lowest on record so far is 20.8°C on Sept 6, 2008,” said an IMD official.The minimum is forecast to hover between 20°C and 22°C over the next two days. The mean minimum temperature this Sept was 25.5°C, up from 24.8°C last Sept.The maximum Tuesday was 32.4°C, over two degrees below normal, up from 28.7°C a day earlier. It is likely to stay between 32 and 34°C Wednesday. The mean maximum temperature this Sept was 34°C, compared with 34.8°C last Sept.Delhi received 79.7 mm of rainfall this month, the lowest recorded in a Sept since 2020, when the city had got just 20.9 mm. This Sept ended with a rainfall deficit of 35.5%, against the entire month’s normal of 123.5 mm. Though there were six rainy days this Sept, only light to moderate showers were logged. There was no ‘heavy rainfall day’ this month.In contrast, Delhi received 136.1 mm rainfall in 2025, 192.5 mm in 2024, 82.7 mm in 2023, 164.5 mm in 2022 and 413.3 mm in 2021.Monsoon retreated from the city on Sept 23, two days before its normal date of withdrawal, with Safdarjung logging 728.6 mm rainfall over the season. Categorised as ‘normal’, it was 16% above the average of 629.7 mm. articles.title: Mumbai man’s family preserves body in freezer for 4 yrs, police stunned
articles.summary: Mumbai police probe legality after an 80-year-old man’s body was kept in a Malad clinic freezer for 4 years; family seeks transfer to a US cryonics centre.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The corpse of an 80-year-old man preserved in a Malad clinic’s freezer for the past four years on the instructions of his family has baffled Mumbai police. They are now consulting experts on the legality of such preservation and its duration, if allowed.The family, who live in Mumbai, told police that they want to move the corpse to a cryonics centre in the US to allow them to preserve it for as long as possible. Police have not filed any formal charges so far.Kurar police visited the polyclinic following a tipoff on Monday night and found the man’s body inside a freezer. The clinic had been shut for the past month for renovation. Police reached out to the man’s family, comprising his elderly wife and adult children. They produced documents showing that the man had died of natural causes in 2022.The children told police that they had been deeply disturbed by his death and wanted to preserve his body for as long as possible. They researched online and came across organisations in the US that offer cryonics, in which legally dead people are preserved at extremely low temperatures, typically using liquid nitrogen. Cryopreservation of cells, tissues and embryos is an established scientific practice, but cryonics is still considered experimental by mainstream scientists.The family began communicating with one such organisation about whether they could move the corpse to the US. They also consulted lawyers in India on the legality of preserving the body here.In the interim, the corpse remained at the clinic, but neither the clinic management nor the family informed local police. Police only learnt about it from locals on Monday night.The property owner, who had rented out the premises for clinic operations since 2022, said he too had not been informed about the body. He told police that he and his family used to visit the clinic to consult a physician whenever someone was unwell.Police recorded the statements of the family members, the clinic management and the property owner on Tuesday. A decision on conducting the man’s final rites is yet to be taken. articles.title: Carney accuses US steelmaker of betraying Canadian workers after layoffs tied to Trump tariffs
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney accused the U.S. owner of steelmaker Stelco, a subsidiary of Cleveland-Cliffs, of betraying Canadian workers Tuesday afte...
articles.body:
TORONTO (AP) — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney accused the U.S. owner of steelmaker Stelco, a subsidiary of Cleveland-Cliffs, of betraying Canadian workers Tuesday after it announced layoffs it attributed in part to U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs — tariffs Cleveland-Cliffs' chief executive has publicly championed.

Carney singled out Cleveland-Cliffs CEO Lourenco Goncalves, noting that he had applauded Trump's steel tariffs. Goncalves has called the 50% tariffs "a necessary step" to protect U.S. steelmakers.

"Our thoughts are with the workers and the families who have been betrayed by the company," Carney said.

Carney also threatened legal action against Cleveland-Cliffs , saying the Ohio-based company has binding employment obligations stemming from its C$3.4 billion ($2.4 billion) takeover of Stelco in 2024.

Stelco said up to 500 workers could be affected as it indefinitely idles cold-rolled and coated operations at its Hamilton, Ontario, plant and shifts production to its Lake Erie facility in Nanticoke, Ontario.

Cleveland-Cliffs said Monday the move does not shift steel production out of Canada: Output will be concentrated at Stelco's Lake Erie Works in Nanticoke, Ontario, where it expects a significant number of affected Hamilton workers to be absorbed, with overall steel tonnage unchanged.

In a memo to employees, Stelco said U.S. tariffs had "significantly shrunk the market" for its cold-rolled and galvanized products. The company said demand in markets it traditionally serves fell almost 25% in the second quarter compared to the 2024 quarterly average, including a 10% decline in Canada.

The layoffs come amid an escalating Canada-U.S. trade war in which Trump has imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian steel and other goods and Canada has retaliated with tariffs of its own. At a White House event Monday announcing a new $15 billion steel plant in Iowa , Trump credited his tariffs with reducing foreign steel imports and attracting investment to the United States, saying companies were building plants there "because they don't want to pay tariffs."

Carney said the federal government had offered financial assistance to preserve jobs but did not disclose the amount or terms.

"There's money on the table from the federal government," Carney said. "The company made representations and has legal obligations for employment. We intend to use all powers that we have and pursue them to the fullest extent of the law."

The Canadian government approved Cleveland-Cliffs' takeover of Stelco in October 2024 on the condition that it meet legally binding five-year employment commitments, including maintaining at least the same number of unionized workers and the vast majority of nonunion employees.

Cleveland-Cliffs did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Carney's remarks.

articles.title: Toddler takes loaded gun to Michigan daycare
articles.summary: Daycare staff members took the gun from the toddler and no one was hurt Monday in Canton Township, a community west of Detroit, police said.
articles.body: Police took a parent into custody this week after a toddler at a Michigan daycare center pulled a loaded handgun in a holster from their backpack, police said. No one was hurt in the incident Monday in Canton Township, and Police Chief Joseph Bialy praised daycare staff members for their handling of the situation. “I’ve watched the video. I’ve seen what their staff did,” he said at a news conference Monday. “And they were prepared and ready to be able to remove this firearm and keep all the kids safe.” Police did not identify the parents, and no criminal charges had been filed by Tuesday afternoon. One of the parents is a law enforcement officer in a neighboring jurisdiction, Bialy said. That was not the parent who was taken into custody, he said. He did not believe the weapon was a service weapon. The firearm — a handgun that was in a holster — came into the building in a backpack, Bialy said. The incident was captured on video that shows the toddler removing the firearm from the backpack, Bialy said. “It’s shocking to see,” he said. A teacher was in the room the entire time, saw what was happening and took swift action to intervene, Bialy said. “Had that not happened, I do not know where we would be right now or what kind of conversation we would be having,” he said. The daycare center has disenrolled the family, NBC affiliate WDIV of Detroit reported. The facility where the incident occurred, Childrens World Early Learning Center, said it would also start searching backpacks entering the building. “We remain committed to ensuring our center is a safe haven for every child and family we serve,” it said. The Wayne County Prosecutor’s Office said Tuesday afternoon that a warrant request was being reviewed but that there would be no arraignment that day. Bialy called the situation a serious incident and said police were treating it that way. He stressed the importance of safe storage of firearms. “I don’t think there was any ill intent by truly anyone involved,” Bialy said. “I think it really falls back on safe security of a firearm.” “The law is clear”: If a child is present or expected to be present, firearms must be secured, he said.

articles.title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after more than 100 allege brain injuries
articles.summary: Hundreds of riders were allegedly injured on X2, which has seats that spin 360 degrees.
articles.body:
Six Flags Magic Mountain, an amusement park in California, has announced it will permanently close a popular rollercoaster after more than 100 riders alleged they suffered brain injuries.

The X2 rollercoaster, one of the park's main attractions, with long wait times to ride and seats that spin 360 degrees, has been closed since July.

Six Flags said the ride had passed a range of safety tests, but that it had decided to retire it because it was "the right thing to do".

The decision comes after lawsuits and news reports alleged that riders suffered brain injuries after riding X2. A law firm representing some of the plaintiffs said the decision had come "too late" for its clients.

Announcing the closure on Tuesday, Six Flags Magic Mountain Park President Brian Oerding said: "Ride safety is a cornerstone of our business, and when we see guest confidence affected, we take it seriously."

Dordick Law Corporation, who filed civil lawsuits against the park, said it had been contacted by about 400 people who alleged they had injuries they believed were caused by the ride.

"They got on X2 expecting a thrill. Instead, they left with catastrophic brain injuries," the firm said in a statement. "Some needed emergency brain surgery. Some are still fighting to get their lives back."

The law firm said that while it welcomed the closure of the ride to protect future guests, "it does nothing for the people who have already been hurt".

Originally called X, the ride first opened in 2002 but was closed months later for repairs to design flaws, the Los Angeles Times reports. It was then closed again in 2007 to replace its trains with lighter versions.

It reopened the following year as X2 and since then has been ridden by more than 16 million people, the park said.

A law firm that represented the family of 22-year-old Christopher Hawley, who died after riding X2 in 2022, said the closure was not enough.

While the Hawley family is "relieved to hear that Six Flags is finally closing the X2, it does not change the fact that Christopher Hawley was killed by a dangerous roller coaster that was allowed to operate for nearly two decades," attorney Brent Wisner of Wisner Baum LLP said in a statement to the BBC.

Hawley's family settled a wrongful death suit with the theme park in August.

"That tragedy cannot be undone," Wisner said, calling for legal reform, proactive regulation and proper governmental oversight.

"We cannot rely on profit-centered corporations to do the right thing only after enough people have been hurt," he added. "We hope that whatever replaces the X2 is safe."

articles.title: As US cozies up to Pakistan, India warns it could impact ties
articles.summary: NEW YOR/ NEW DELHI: Amid growing US-Pakistan bonhomie, external affairs minister S Jaishankar warned that a lack of understanding about India’s concerns
articles.body: NEW YOR/ NEW DELHI: Amid growing US-Pakistan bonhomie, external affairs minister S Jaishankar warned that a lack of understanding about India’s concerns over cross-border terrorism will affect India-US bilateral ties.Flagging issues pertaining to each other’s sensitivities, the minister said that terrorism was of particular importance to India.“There are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbour as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many, many decades,” Jaishankar said, without naming Pakistan.“Now, if something which matters so deeply to us, there isn’t enough understanding or appreciation or empathy of that, I think that creates a problem too. That you know if... one of my primary concerns is not fully appreciated by my partner, then clearly there is an impact of that on the relationship,” he said, alluding to India-US ties.Jaishankar’s remarks followed US President Donald Trump’s sharing on social media a video clip of Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif’s UNGA speech where he thanked the president for his “timely intervention” to end India’s Op Sindoor. Jaishankar was speaking at the Asia Society Policy Institute where he was asked about the state of the bilateral relationship amid differences over trade and tariffs.The minister said that the trade deal both sides are finalising can improve relations, but added that the period it took to reach the understanding created bumps in the relationship.S Jaishankar: Delay in reaching trade deal created bumps in relationshipBear in mind, India is a society of small producers, small agriculture producers, small factories. Apart from the per capita gap between India and the US, the nature of production, nature of society is very different,” he said.“A trade negotiation required a certain amount of ... patience and detailing to see it through… The expectation that it could rapidly move forward, I think, was tested against a ground reality which was much more complex,” added the minister.Jaishankar said that “today, we have reached a situation where there is more or less an understanding on the trade agreement”.India and the US had in Feb announced the finalisation of the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement. However, changes in the US tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.The two sides have since continued negotiations on their bilateral trade agreement amid the changes in the US tariff regime. Jaishankar, alluding to comments by commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal, said the issue now was what had changed on the American side and how the new Section 301 process would affect the agreement. “The 301 process is still in the works, it’s still unfolding. So the issue for us is at what point do you close out an agreement which is very, very far advanced,” Jaishankar said.“But the period that it took to reach it, that did create bumps last year for the relationship. So presumably, if that agreement is closed out, that would be one point which would contribute to a better relationship,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Household energy bills forecast to see biggest rise in four years
articles.summary: A typical household faces an annual gas and electricity bill of £1,999 from January, based on a key forecast.
articles.body:
Household energy prices are set to soar in January, with a typical annual bill forecast to jump by £276, figures shared with the BBC reveal.

The 16% predicted increase would hit millions of households at the coldest time of year, and would mark the biggest rise in bills for four years.

The forecast from consultancy Cornwall Insight comes a day before prices go up under regulator Ofgem's October price cap and puts increased pressure on the government to support those who will struggle to pay.

Meanwhile, the boss of supplier EDF Simone Rossi has warned the UK is "walking into a second energy crisis" and called for an extension to the VAT cut on electricity which kicks in on Thursday.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham told BBC Radio 4's Today programme he would not call Rossi's crisis warning an overstatement, adding that the cost of home energy, as well as petrol and diesel, was "very difficult indeed".

Speaking from the Labour conference in Liverpool, he added: "We're looking at any measure that can give people breathing space, that can take the pressure off."

About 20 million households in England, Scotland and Wales are on variable energy tariffs set by Ofgem's price cap, which puts a maximum price on each unit of gas and electricity.

Those homes will see a 4% increase in prices on Thursday, the equivalent of about £60 per year – or £5 per month – taking an annual bill to £1,723 for the typical household using both electricity and gas and paying by direct debit if this level was sustained for a year.

That rise would have been higher without the government's VAT cut, which knocks the equivalent of about £45 a year off a typical bill.

But forecasts show a far greater increase is possible for bills in January. Cornwall Insight said its latest forecast suggests the typical annual bill would rise to £1,999.

The forecast 16% rise will come at the worst time of year, according to Craig Lowrey, principal consultant at Cornwall Insight.

"These prices are going to hit households hard. January is already a difficult month for many, with cold weather and bank balances still recovering from Christmas," he said.

The predicted rise is the result of disruption of gas supplies owing to the conflict in the Middle East, and the resulting low gas storage levels in Europe. Rebuilding those stocks could mean high bills "well beyond the winter", the forecaster said.

Cornwall Insight has a strong track record on forecasts and is widely respected across the industry and politics. Similar forecasts have been made by energy suppliers.

What will the energy cap changes mean for my bills?

Four ways to keep your energy bills down

This remains only a prediction at this stage. Ofgem will not announce the actual January price change until late November.

While an easing of tensions in the Middle East could lessen the pain for billpayers, the price setting period for the January cap is already halfway through.

With little sign of a truce or lower international energy costs, a big increase in prices for those not on a fixed tariff looks highly likely. Lowrey said a January rise was "all but certain".

That will be tough for people like Aaron Richards from Maidenhead.

"I try to eat less takeaways, work more overtime, and try to budget a bit better, but at the same time, we shouldn't have to," he said.

Aaron drives a diesel car, and so is paying record high prices to travel to and from work.

"I just feel like everything's going up. How far is it going to go? Someone's got to step in," he said.

"I know people who can't afford to heat their house and they're struggling at the moment. Housing and eating are two of life's essentials that everyone should have. It shouldn't be a challenge to have any of those things."

Years of relatively high domestic energy bills have left some people facing big sums in unpaid bills.

Recent data from Ofgem showed that customers collectively owe more than £5bn in unpaid bills and charges to suppliers.

The regulator has a proposed debt relief scheme on the table, and campaigners keep telling them to get on with it, urging the government to provide funding for it to be implemented.

"This is unsustainable, not just for households but also for the market as a whole," said Adam Scorer, chief executive of fuel poverty charity National Energy Action.

"The Budget must deliver additional targeted support for households most at risk this winter, alongside action to tackle energy debt and improve the least energy-efficient homes."

Among others calling for government help for struggling billpayers is Simone Rossi, chief executive of supplier EDF Energy.

Speaking exclusively to the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast, Mr Rossi said: "We are actually walking into a second significant energy crisis after the one we experienced just four years ago."

He said that the government should extend the cut in VAT on electricity bills from 5% to 0% beyond April, when it is due to expire.

He also urged ministers to give the go-ahead to the new Jackdaw gas field off the coast of Aberdeen, and the Rosebank oil field off Shetland.

The government has consistently said that it will consider ways to offer breathing space to billpayers on the cost of living.

Additional reporting by Oliver Smith and Paul Seddon. Graphics by Miguel Roca-Terry.

articles.title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all conventional food
articles.summary: The advertising watchdog said that viewers could assume from the ad that replacing all normal food with Huel was "nutritionally appropriate".
articles.body:
An advert for Huel meal replacement shakes has been banned by the advertising watchdog for encouraging or condoning "irresponsible" dietary practices.

The ad featured Huel brand ambassador Spencer Matthews sharing an anecdote of a person he met who "only eats Huel" and who won a 260km race "by miles".

The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) said that viewers could assume from the ad that replacing all conventional food with Huel was "nutritionally appropriate" and was compatible with elite physical performance.

Huel said Matthews' anecdote was not "a recommendation or instruction" and the purpose of the ad was to challenge the misconception that Huel could replace every meal".

The video, which appeared as a sponsored Instagram post and YouTube pre-roll ad, featured Matthews speaking to Huel founder Julian Hearn in the style of a podcast.

The Instagram post included the caption: "Here's how our founder uses Huel. Spoiler alert it's not for every meal."

In the video Hearn said that he has Huel products for breakfast and lunch during the working week, but has a "traditional meal" when he goes home.

In response, Matthews said that when he was competing in an ultramarathon, he met a man who "only eats Huel".

Matthews said he was initially sceptical that the man would be able to manage the race, but then said: "He won it by miles, like literally just left us all in the dirt."

Hearn replied: "In an ideal world, you should have nutritionally complete whole food.

"Most people either don't do that or can't have the time to do that, and therefore that's where Huel fits in the gap."

Huel, which is based in Hertfordshire, was founded by Hearn in 2015. It is currently in the process of being bought by French conglomerate Danone .

The market for so-called complete nutrition products, aimed at time-poor, health-conscious consumers, is thought to be worth $5.9bn (£4.4bn).

The ASA received four complaints about the advert, which challenged whether the content was irresponsible. Two of the complainants also challenged whether the health claims in the ad breached the ASA's advertising code.

The ASA acknowledged in its ruling that the ad "did not explicitly recommend that consumers replace all conventional foods with Huel", but consumers could nonetheless interpret the anecdote as "an acceptable dietary practice".

"By presenting exclusive consumption of Huel in that context, the ads suggested that the complete replacement of conventional food with Huel was nutritionally appropriate and presented no barrier to achieving a high level of physical performance," the ruling said.

The ASA also upheld the complaint regarding the health claims as it ruled Matthews' anecdote about the ultramarathon athlete "implied a beneficial relationship between consuming Huel and the ability to sustain exceptionally high levels of physical and endurance performance".

In its response to the complaints, Huel said the advert "unambiguously positioned Huel as part of a balanced diet for occasions when preparing whole food was not practicable".

The company pointed to Matthews reacting with "extreme scepticism and disbelief" to the idea of a person solely consuming Huel.

"The anecdote was recounted as a remarkable and unexpected occurrence, not as a representative outcome or a recommendation or instruction to consumers to replicate.

"At no point in the ads did either speaker suggest that consumers should adopt a 100% Huel diet."

It is not the first time that Huel has landed in hot water with the ASA over the use of its products as a replacement for conventional food.

Additionally, some experts have questioned the effectiveness of replacing meals with nutritionally rich drinks.

Huel told BBC News that it had complied with the ASA ruling.

"We do not position Huel as a complete diet replacement or claim that it improves athletic performance," a spokesperson said.

articles.title: Carville mocks Dem candidate staffers as 'weak' and 'soft' for complaining about treatment to New York Times
articles.summary: James Carville unleashed a profanity-laced video defending Mary Peltola after staffers complained to the New York Times about her alleged actions.
articles.body: Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville blasted staffers who complained to The New York Times about working for former Alaska Rep. Mary Peltola as she runs for the Senate. The Times article, "Angry Outbursts, Slurs and Firings: Tumult Rocks a Key Senate Campaign," featured comments from former aides who described chaos in Peltola's congressional office and Senate campaign as the Democrat hopes to flip a Republican seat. "I want to react to a story I read in The New York Times concerning the Democratic nominee for the United States Senate from the state of Alaska," Carville said in a brief video posted to the Politicon channel Monday. "It would appear that we have some upset little staffers that she is not — when she's under pressure — not nice to ‘em. "Of course, The New York Times didn't understand when you're in the middle of a political campaign, and you're a candidate, and you're under pressure, and you got everything coming in from everywhere, and you're trying to raise money, and you're trying to fend off attacks, and you're trying to do this, maybe you don't have time to be overly courteous to little pussified staffers that just — they — 'I want my name and my humanity,’" he continued. GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING "I got news for you. When I ran campaigns, you didn't have a f---in’ name until you did something," Carville said. "'Hey, you, come over here! Do this! Do what the f--- you’re told and shut up!’ And you know what? Then, when you achieve something, or you do something, then you get a name. But until that, in politics, you don't have a name. Go do something else. Go be a social worker. They'll give you a name right away. "Now, if somebody does something obviously dehumanizing or overly rude, then that's one thing," Carville added, juxtaposing that with "Telling people to go get coffee for you or calling them by, ‘Hey, you.’ Everybody wants a pronoun. Well, I'll give you a pronoun. ‘You’ or ‘a--hole come over here.’" He went on to mock various demands that employees might have, replying, "Well s---, that’s why we lose." He also suggested that female political candidates are scrutinized more heavily when accused of lashing out at staffers. articles.title: Debate do governo do DF na Globo: assista à íntegra das falas | G1
articles.standfirst: Debate contou com a presença de Kiko Caputo (Novo), Leandro Grass (PT), Paula Belmonte (PSDB) e Ricardo Cappelli (PSB).
articles.summary: Assista à íntegra do debate entre os candidatos ao governo do DF na Globo e confira as propostas de Grass, Caputo, Belmonte e Cappelli para as Eleições 2026.
articles.body:
A TV Globo realizou um debate com os candidatos ao governo do Distrito Federal, na noite desta terça-feira (29), em Brasília .

O debate contou com a presença de Kiko Caputo ( Novo ) , Leandro Grass ( PT ) , Paula Belmonte ( PSDB ) e Ricardo Cappelli ( PSB ) — em ordem alfabética. A mediação foi realizada pelo jornalista Heraldo Pereira.

A candidata e atual governadora Celina Leão ( PP ) foi convidada, mas optou por não participar .

Candidatos ao governo do DF posicionados para debate na TV Globo — Foto: Bruna Yamaguti/g1

➡️ A participação de Kiko Caputo foi determinada em uma decisão do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) nesta terça-feira (29) . O presidente da Corte, ministro Nunes Marques , atendeu a um pedido de liminar do Novo, alterando entendimento anterior do TSE que regulamenta os critérios de participação de partidos em debates eleitorais em emissoras de rádio e TV.

➡️A decisão liminar garante a participação dos candidatos do Partido Novo nos debates das Eleições de 2026 em todas as emissoras de rádio e TV a partir desta terça.

➡️ O ex-governador José Roberto Arruda (PSD) chegou a ser convidado para o debate, mas teve a candidatura barrada pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) de forma definitiva na sexta-feira (25). A decisão proibiu que o político participe de eventos eleitorais, como o debate.

Veja a íntegra no topo deste texto – e, abaixo, todas as participações dos candidatos.

Leandro Grass (PT) para Kiko Caputo (Novo)

Kiko Caputo (Novo) para Paula Belmonte (PSDB)

Paula Belmonte (PSDB) para Ricardo Cappelli (PSB)

Ricardo Cappelli (PSB) para Leandro Grass (PT)

A última interação do segundo bloco foi entre os candidatos Ricardo Cappelli e Kiko Caputo.

“Passamos da meia-noite e você está aqui porque se preocupa com a nossa cidade, com a nossa vida, com a sua família, com aquilo que está acontecendo. A Celina não veio. A Celina não veio aqui, a Celina não foi ao hospital, a Celina não foi à escola, a Celina não foi ao transporte. Ela abandonou o Distrito Federal, por isso que ela não está aqui. Ela não tem condições de governar mais essa cidade. Foi o pior governo da história.

Você merece uma chance, Brasília merece uma chance. Vamos dar uma chance para Brasília, vamos dar uma oportunidade para a nossa cidade, para aquela criança que está passando fome e para aquela mãe atípica que não tem vaga na creche, na escola. Vamos dar uma vaga para aquela pessoa que está esperando há muito, muito tempo para poder ter um atendimento na saúde. Eu sou o Leandro Grass, sou professor brasiliense, tenho 41 anos, a minha vida toda foi aqui, inteirinha. Fui professor da rede pública, da rede privada, fui deputado distrital, sou gestor, sociólogo, presidi uma das maiores instituições do Brasil.

Tenho experiência, sei o que eu quero fazer e sei porque eu sou candidato. Porque eu não tolero, eu não me conformo com o sofrimento das pessoas na cidade que eu amo, na cidade em que eu nasci. Por isso, eu peço o seu voto. Vá à urna domingo, vote, não fique em casa, não vote nulo. Vá, escolha."

"Eu sou fruto de um DF que funcionava. Estudei em escola pública, me tratava na saúde pública. Aqui eu pude estudar, construir minha família e prosperar. E eu quero que você também tenha essa oportunidade, que seus filhos, seus netos também vejam Brasília como uma terra de oportunidades. Para isso, a gente precisa dar um choque de honestidade nesse governo. A gente precisa colocar gestão na administração pública para que a política volte a resolver os problemas reais da nossa população. Eu sou ficha limpa e eu estou aqui para servir você.

Eu quero ser o melhor servidor público do Distrito Federal. O Distrito Federal já teve educação de qualidade, saúde de qualidade, mas nós podemos ter esperança. Porque dinheiro tem, o que está faltando é vergonha na cara de quem administra, dessa velha política que já governou o DF, fabricou uma série de escândalos e nos colocou nas páginas policiais.

Eu quero voltar a tratar a sua família com dignidade e respeito. Então, se você quer resgatar o sonho de JK e fazer disso aqui de novo a capital da esperança, a saída é Kiko Caputo.”

"Eu quero agradecer muito a Deus por essa noite iluminada, e quero te pedir mais um pouquinho de atenção para você entender o que está acontecendo.

A Celina não veio aqui. Ela tirou o Ibaneis, tirou o Arruda e está contando que já ganhou a eleição porque o candidato que está em segundo lugar, ela sabe que vai perder dela no segundo turno. Só que 50% da população do Distrito Federal ainda não decidiu em quem votar. Então, meu irmão, essa eleição, daqui a quatro dias, está na sua mão. Na hora da urna, é só você e Deus. E você pode mudar o Distrito Federal. Eu sou o Cappelli. Eu estou aqui há 23 anos.

Eles me chamam de forasteiro. Eu sou igual a você. Você que veio da Bahia, do Maranhão, do Piauí, do Ceará, que veio de Sergipe, veio de Minas. Eu sou igual às pessoas que são aqui do Distrito Federal, nascidas aqui, mas que trabalham duro desde cedo.

Fizeram de tudo para eu desistir. Cortaram meu dinheiro, botaram pessoas grandes para me pressionar, mas eu não desisto. Sabe por quê? Porque eu sou igual a você. Você quando chega no ponto de ônibus às 5:30 da manhã, você não tem o direito de desistir. Eu, quando comecei a trabalhar com 18 anos na rua, não tive o direito de desistir. E eu vou até o final para a gente mudar o Distrito Federal.

Vem comigo, me dá uma chance para a gente mudar o Distrito Federal. Muito obrigado, candidato Cappelli."

"Primeiro, eu peço a Deus que nos abençoe. Nós estamos talvez no momento mais importante de uma eleição, quem vai governar o Distrito Federal daqui quatro anos. Nós precisamos estar na rua hoje, amanhã, depois de amanhã, juntos, para mostrar que tem uma alternativa. Ao doutor Everardo, que é o meu vice, que vai comandar o governo sem corrupção, combatendo a corrupção.

Mas agora eu peço, nos 45 segundos que me restam, mostrar quem eu sou. Eu sou Paula Belmonte. Eu sou mãe de seis filhos, entrei na política porque eu vivo nessa cidade e conheço essa cidade com uma palma da mão. Eu conheço a realidade das escolas, eu conheço a realidade dos hospitais e aqui eu estou sozinha, sem muito partido, só o meu partido.

Mas com o povo, minha coligação é com você, a única mulher que tem condições e que não é omissa, de vencer essa governadora atual. Então eu peço para que você nos acompanhe e mais do que isso, amanhã fale para o seu vizinho, para o seu amigo. Existe sim uma candidata ao governo do Distrito Federal, Paula Belmonte."

articles.title: PIS/Pasep esquecido: prazo para pedir ressarcimento acaba hoje | G1
articles.standfirst: Trabalhadores que fizerem a solicitação até esta quarta (30) recebem os pagamentos no dia 26 de outubro. Consulta pode ser feita pelo site Repis Cidadão ou app do FGTS.
articles.summary: Trabalhadores que fizerem a solicitação até esta quarta (30) recebem os pagamentos no dia 26 de outubro. Consulta pode ser feita pelo site Repis Cidadão ou app do FGTS.
articles.body:
PIS/Pasep, FGTS - Saque — Foto: José Cruz/Agência Brasil

Termina nesta quarta-feira (30) o prazo para solicitar o segundo lote de pagamentos do antigo fundo PIS/Pasep. O saque para quem fizer o pedido dentro do prazo está previsto para o dia 26 de outubro.

Ao longo do ano, há outras datas para solicitações e pagamentos, seguindo um calendário já estabelecido pela Caixa Econômica Federal .

🔎 O antigo fundo PIS/Pasep era usado para incrementar a renda de trabalhadores com carteira assinada e servidores públicos entre 1971 e 1988. Ele é diferente do abono salarial PIS/Pasep pago atualmente .

O trabalhador pode checar se tem valores a receber por meio do site Repis Cidadão ou pelo aplicativo do FGTS .

Segundo o governo, o saldo médio disponível para saque é de R$ 2,8 mil por pessoa, mas o montante varia conforme o tempo trabalhado e o salário recebido na época. Os valores estão corrigidos pela inflação.

A plataforma Repis Cidadão também ensina o procedimento para retirar o dinheiro, inclusive com orientações específicas para herdeiros , no caso de falecimento do beneficiário. Para acessá-la, é necessário ter conta gov.br nos níveis prata ou ouro.

Se o ressarcimento não for solicitado até setembro de 2028, os valores serão definitivamente incorporados ao Tesouro Nacional , sem possibilidade de saque.

Como consultar se tenho dinheiro esquecido?

1. Como consultar se tenho dinheiro esquecido?

REPIS Cidadão, site lançado pelo Ministério da Fazenda para facilitar consulta e saque do antigo PIS/Pasep — Foto: Reprodução

Clique em "entrar com gov.br" . Se você não tiver uma conta no sistema do governo federal, veja aqui como fazer ;

Faça login com seu CPF e senha, e clique em "autorizar" ;

Informe o NIS (Número de Identificação Social) do beneficiário. O número é o mesmo do PIS e pode ser encontrado em vários lugares (leia mais abaixo) ;

Clique em "pesquisar" . E, se você tiver valores a receber, o site vai orientá-lo sobre as próximas etapas.

NIS é a sigla para Número de Identificação Social. O documento é uma sequência de 11 dígitos disponibilizada pela Caixa Econômica Federal.

Esse cadastro é necessário tanto para quem trabalha com carteira assinada como para quem quer ter acesso a programas sociais, como o Bolsa Família.

Os números do NIS e do PIS (Programa de Integração Social) são os mesmos . A diferença está na origem deles: enquanto o NIS é gerado no momento em que alguém passa a usar benefícios sociais, o PIS é gerado quando a carteira de trabalho é assinada pela primeira vez.

O NIS pode ser consultado tanto de forma física quanto digital em diversos canais do governo. Veja a seguir:

Extrato do FGTS: é possível conferir o número do PIS dentro de um dos contratos registrados no aplicativo.

Cartão Cidadão: o número do NIS está identificado logo abaixo do nome do beneficiário e acima da data de emissão do cartão.

Meu INSS: no site , o número do NIS aparece como NIT, na parte dos dados cadastrais. A consulta também pode ser feita pelo telefone da Previdência Social (135), de segunda a sábado, das 7h às 22h.

CadÚnico: é possível encontrar o NIS após preencher informações pessoais no site CadÚnico ou pelo aplicativo.

O trabalhador pode protocolar o pedido de ressarcimento em uma agência da Caixa Econômica Federal ou fazer a solicitação pelo aplicativo do FGTS .

Ele vai precisar fazer login no app, acessar a opção "mais", "ressarcimento PIS/Pasep" e seguir as orientações para anexar os documentos exigidos.

Se o pedido for feito pelo próprio beneficiário, basta que ele tenha em mãos um documento de identidade oficial.

Já no caso de herdeiros, será necessário apresentar:

Certidão PIS/PASEP/FGTS emitida pela Previdência Social com a relação de dependentes habilitados à pensão por morte; ou

Declaração de dependentes habilitados à pensão emitida pelo órgão pagador do benefício; ou

Autorização judicial ou escritura pública assinada por todos os dependentes e sucessores, se capazes e concordantes, atestando por escrito a autorização do saque e declarando não haver outros dependentes ou sucessores conhecidos.

Após a solicitação, a Caixa vai analisar o pedido e enviar as informações ao Ministério da Fazenda . O pagamento será realizado diretamente na conta bancária do interessado na Caixa ou por meio de conta poupança social digital, de acordo com o calendário a seguir.

O Programa de Integração Social (PIS) foi criado em 1970 para incrementar a poupança individual dos trabalhadores do setor privado.

Logo depois, o Programa de Formação do Patrimônio do Servidor Público (PASEP) foi lançado para servidores públicos civis e militares, inspirado no mesmo princípio.

Em 1975, os recursos dos dois programas foram transferidos para um único fundo: o Fundo PIS-Pasep, que parou de funcionar 1988, quando foi substituído pelo abono salarial atual.

Em 2020, as cotas do fundo que não haviam sido sacadas foram transferidas para o Fundo de Garantia do Tempo de Serviço (FGTS) e, três anos depois, para uma conta única do Tesouro Nacional .

Desde então, a Caixa abriu para que os trabalhadores com dinheiro esquecido na conta peçam o ressarcimento dos valores.

▶️ O abono salarial atual — uma espécie de 14º salário, no valor de até um salário mínimo — é pago anualmente a trabalhadores com carteira assinada e servidores públicos que atendem aos requisitos do programa.

articles.title: Da situação de rua a dono de app: empreendedor cria 'rival' de Uber e fatura R$ 120 mil por mês | G1
articles.standfirst: Sérgio Brito trabalhou oito meses, 12 horas por dia, para juntar os R$ 35 mil do investimento inicial. Hoje, aplicativo opera em seis cidades.
articles.summary: Sérgio Brito trabalhou oito meses, 12 horas por dia, para juntar os R$ 35 mil do investimento inicial. Hoje, aplicativo opera em seis cidades.
articles.body:
O empreendedor Sergio Brito criou um aplicativo de transporte que funciona em Araxá , interior de Minas Gerais, e em outras cinco cidades. A plataforma, lançada em 2022, é formada por uma frota de 170 veículos.

Quem vê o sucesso do empresário, não imagina as dificuldades que ele enfrentou ao longo da vida. Antes de empreender, ele viveu no interior de São Paulo, mas deixou o estado para trabalhar na colheita de café em Minas Gerais.

No campo, ele encontrou condições de trabalho precárias e decidiu deixar o local . "Eu passei quase três anos morando na rua", lembra.

Apesar disso, Sérgio só retornou para a casa após ser encontrado pela família dele. "Eu queria voltar como vencedor", diz.

A mudança de vida do empreendedor veio por meio de um concurso de modelos em Franca (SP). Ele ficou em 2º lugar e ganhou um curso de gastronomia, o que fez com que trabalhasse por sete anos em um hotel de Araxá.

Durante a pandemia de Covid-19, no entanto, Sérgio acabou perdendo o emprego e virou motorista de aplicativo. A partir de então, não demorou muito para o empresário ter a ideia de criar a própria plataforma de transportes. Com o objetivo traçado, estudou tudo o que podia sobre tecnologia para desenvolver o aplicativo.

💸 O investimento inicial foi de R$ 35 mil. Para levantar o valor, Sérgio passou oito meses rodando 12 horas por dia.

Agora, empresário fatura R$ 120 mil por mês. O êxito do aplicativo de viagens é explicado pelas vantagens oferecidas aos condutores parceiros , como:

carro de apoio em acidentes e pneu furado.

O último benefício é acionado pelo próprio motorista, através de uma central.

Além de Araxá, o aplicativo está disponível nas cidades de Sacramento , Ibiá , Monte Carmelo , Catalão e Patos de Minas .

Para os motoristas parceiros, é cobrada uma taxa fixa de 15% do valor das corridas. Em outros aplicativos, essa taxa costuma ser de até 40%.

"Ele [o motorista] vai ligar para a central e a central vai mandar um carro de apoio (...) É por isso que hoje existem mil e cem motoristas na fila de espera", explica Sérgio.

🚗 Segundo o dono do negócio, mais de 1.100 mil motoristas estão na fila de espera para utilizar o aplicativo.

articles.title: "Made him a target for verbal attack and physical threats": Candace Owens sued by Utah man over alleged Charlie Kirk shooting accusations
articles.summary: A Utah man who says he was simply attending Charlie Kirk’s 2026 rally has filed a lawsuit against political commentator Candace Owens, alleging that her
articles.body: A Utah man who says he was simply attending Charlie Kirk’s 2026 rally has filed a lawsuit against political commentator Candace Owens, alleging that her podcast coverage falsely tied him to Kirk’s killing. Robert Hild Jr. claims the accusations turned his life upside down, damaged his reputation and exposed his family to unwanted attention and threats. The lawsuit, filed Monday, also details how social media posts and photographs were allegedly used to support claims against him. Hild says he has repeatedly sought a retraction, but the disputed statements continued to circulate among Owens’ audience.Utah man details alleged fallout from Candace Owens claimsHild was present at the Utah Valley University event on Sept. 10, 2026, when Kirk was fatally shot. According to the lawsuit, he witnessed the attack and later took shelter at the home of his friend’s grandmother with others who had been at the rally.The case says the situation changed after photographs emerged showing alleged shooter Tyler Robinson near the home where Hild and his companions had stayed. The FBI later released a separate image of Robinson inside a stairwell on the UVU campus.Hild argues that those circumstances were misinterpreted. The lawsuit says he, his friend and a roommate later walked along a trail Robinson was believed to have taken and took selfies. A friend subsequently shared those images online.According to Hild, Owens used those social media photographs during her podcast coverage and suggested that he had a connection to the suspect. The lawsuit says she also alleged that Hild had ties to foreign actors and a Ukrainian military group with alleged links to neo-Nazis.Charlie Kirk shooting claims allegedly led to threatsThe lawsuit says Hild attempted to persuade Owens to correct or withdraw the allegations, but claims she declined. It further alleges that Owens continued discussing him despite people providing information about his presence at the rally.The fallout, Hild says, went beyond online criticism. He claims followers shared personal information about him and members of his family, including names and home addresses. The lawsuit also alleges that his home and vehicle were vandalized.Hild says the situation became serious enough that law enforcement advised him and his roommates not to remain at their home.In the lawsuit, Hild describes himself as a "private citizen who was in the process of building a happy and productive life far from the public spotlight." He also says he "experienced the trauma of watching a horrific murder up close."The legal complaint alleges that the claims have "upended his life, irreparably damaged his reputation, and made him a target for verbal attack and physical threats."The allegations in the lawsuit remain claims at this stage. articles.title: ​In a first, government admits in SC problem of exorbitant pricing of drugs, promises fix
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With Supreme Court toughening its stand against poor patients being forced to pay exorbitant prices for medicines, govt on Tuesday admitted
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With Supreme Court toughening its stand against poor patients being forced to pay exorbitant prices for medicines, govt on Tuesday admitted that there was a problem and assured the court it would make efforts to address it.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said there was no rationale for controlling the price of a few scheduled medicines and allowing the rest to be sold at inflated prices as all medicines are essential. It suggested a uniform rule limiting the MRP to not more than 16% above the price to the retailer (PTR).SG Tushar Mehta told SC that he had discussed the issue with official concerned. Govt was not taking an adversarial stand on it, he said, seeking time for further consultations to find a solution. “We will have to find a way out. Some way that balances equities... let me sit with officers and then respond,” he said.The court said taxpayers’ money was also wasted because of exorbitant medicine prices as corporate hospitals obtain full reimbursement for inflated MRPs when patients undergo treatment under govt-sponsored welfare schemes, with the money being paid from the exchequer.“It affects society. Pharma companies are not bothered about it. Why do they fix MRP at high prices? This is carnage... Corporate hospitals are not going to spare anyone, and they will charge the price at MRP. Why should common man suffer like this?” SC asked.After the hearing, the SC adjourned the case for Oct 12.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW YORK: The ties between India and China are “better” today than they were a couple of years ago, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said, underlining that as border issues are resolved, the relationship returns to normalcy.He was responding to a question on India-China relations, which have seen an upswing in recent times, including President Xi Jinping’s recent visit to India for the Brics Leaders’ Summit hosted by New Delhi.“If you asked me, compared to where you were in 2025, is the relationship better today? I would say yes. Compared to 2024, even more so,” Jaishankar said during a conversation hosted at Asia Society on Monday. He said it was not so much a “structural change”, but part of the reason things had improved was that “they had gone so much off-track that the moment you stabilised it, it was going to improve”. After the 2020 border standoff, the relationship had been impacted, he said.Following the standoff, all “normal contacts” between the two nations had halted, though “trade was continuing”. articles.title: Repeat offender with lengthy rap sheet accused of gunning down Kentucky trooper during traffic stop
articles.summary: Emonnie Branch was on probation for securities fraud and wanted for a violation before the traffic stop that left Trooper Hayden Phillips dead.
articles.body: The Tennessee man accused of killing a Kentucky state trooper was on probation and already wanted for a violation, with a criminal record that included assault, fraud and illegally possessing a gun. Emonnie Branch, 51, was denied bond Tuesday on a charge of murder of a first responder in the death of Trooper Hayden Phillips, a husband and father of three young boys. Tennessee Department of Correction records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Branch was serving five years of probation for a fraud-related conviction. His supervision was scheduled to end in July 2030. Sumner County District Attorney Thomas Dean told Fox 17 Nashville that Branch was already wanted for a probation violation tied to his securities fraud conviction before Monday’s shooting. CALIFORNIA GUNMAN REPEATEDLY RELEASED BEFORE DEADLY RAMPAGE, FIERY SHOOTOUT WITH DEPUTIES "Looks like he has a very extensive and varied criminal history," Commonwealth’s Attorney Kori Bumgarner said during Tuesday’s arraignment, the outlet reported. CHARLOTTE REPEAT OFFENDER CHARGED WITH KILLING MAN HOURS AFTER RELEASE ON BOND Dean said Branch’s prior convictions included attempted domestic assault, violating a no-contact order and securities fraud. Court records reviewed by the outlet also showed a 2009 conviction for illegally possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. Fox 17 reported that Branch was arrested twice this year for probation violations. Warren County Regional Jail records reviewed by Fox News Digital show he is being held without bond on the murder charge and a fugitive charge. SUSPECTS AT LARGE AFTER TUCSON POLICE RECRUIT KILLED, PIMA COUNTY CORRECTIONS OFFICER WOUNDED IN SHOOTING Phillips was shot and killed during a traffic stop on Interstate 65 in Warren County Monday, Kentucky State Police said. Authorities identified Branch as the suspect and issued a statewide Blue Alert before Louisville Metro Police captured him that evening. "He was senselessly murdered," U.S. Attorney Kyle Bumgarner said Monday night during a news briefing. "We have a wife that expected her husband to come home. We have three little boys who don’t have a dad." JURY CONVICTS KEVIN SALAZAR IN EXECUTION-STYLE KILLING OF LA DEPUTY RYAN CLINKUNBROOMER "One of our own was gunned down and murdered on the side of the road," Kyle Bumgarner added. He pledged that the Justice Department would give state prosecutors and investigators "every tool" and "every bit of support" it could to help them pursue the maximum sentence. Kentucky State Police Commissioner Col. Phillip Burnett Jr. condemned the suspect’s "cowardly actions" and explained why he had mentioned his name only once. "I want you to know I only mentioned his name one time," Burnett said. AMERICA'S WOUNDED COPS FIND HOPE, HEALING AND SECOND CHANCE THROUGH OFFICERS WHO REFUSE TO LEAVE THEM BEHIND "We will seek justice for Hayden," he continued. "Let me repeat that, we will seek justice for Hayden. We will not rest until this happens." Phillips was a three-year state police veteran assigned to Post 3 in Bowling Green. Burnett promised his family the agency would stand beside them. "You will not walk this path alone," he said. Phillips’ wife, Jordan, shared her grief Tuesday. DRUNK WRONG-WAY DRIVER KILLED MASS TROOPER AFTER 9 DRINKS AT BAR, DA REPORT SAYS "I’ve laid here all night waiting for him to come home… for the radio to click off, the gun belt to hang," she wrote on Facebook. "I promise to pick up all the pieces and force myself to carry on for your boys. I know you would want me to," she added. State police escorted Phillips’ body to Glasgow Tuesday. A candlelight vigil is scheduled for Thursday at 6:30 p.m. local time. Gov. Andy Beshear ordered flags at all state buildings lowered to half-staff from sunrise to sunset Sunday, Oct. 4, in honor of Phillips. "Trooper Hayden Phillips was a hero who sacrificed everything protecting our people and our commonwealth, and it is our sacred duty to honor him and his family," Beshear said. He urged Kentuckians to pray for Jordan and their three children and encouraged donations to the Kentucky State Police Foundation, saying all proceeds would go directly to the family. articles.title: ‘Almost like a constitution’: Trump, top US tech CEOs sign AI safety pact
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump and the heads of some of the biggest US technology and artificial intelligence companies have signed a voluntary “morally
articles.body: US president Donald Trump and the heads of some of the biggest US technology and artificial intelligence companies have signed a voluntary “morally binding” accord aimed at putting stronger safety controls around the development and deployment of AI.Trump announced the Joint Commitment On Frontier Responsibilities after a White House luncheon with leading tech executives, describing the agreement as “almost like a constitution”. The one-page accord lays out four layers of internal and external controls, including independent audits and board-level oversight of AI safety systems.The agreement comes as the Trump administration continues to promote rapid AI development while facing growing concerns over the technology’s potential risks. Trump has repeatedly rejected calls for broad “guardrails”, arguing that restricting AI would undermine US economic growth and its race with China. ‘Almost like a constitution’“It’s almost like a constitution in a way, and the biggest ?people in the world signed that, and ?I signed it as president, and it really ?is a form of protection,” Trump said.The accord was signed by Trump, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Elon Musk, founder of xAI, which is now part of SpaceX.Trump said the agreement would allow for “tremendous self-policing” within the industry and described it as “morally binding”. He said about 10 people would be named to a committee to “watch over the whole enterprise”, with a person also expected to be appointed to oversee the agreement after consultations with industry.The document does not impose legal requirements or specify penalties for companies that fail to comply. Instead, it sets out voluntary commitments and leaves open the possibility of future regulation.“Over time, it may make sense to codify these steps into laws and regulations,” the accord said.The participating companies also agreed to meet regularly to establish safety standards and best practices for their AI systems.Four layers of AI safeguardsThe accord calls for companies to establish “robust internal controls” to monitor AI models during training and deployment, particularly in areas involving cybersecurity, biosecurity and chemical threats. The controls are also intended to ensure models do not hack or access technical systems in unintended ways.A second layer requires internal teams to verify that the companies’ monitoring, detection and other safety controls are functioning as intended.The third layer involves an “independent external auditor” assessing whether those controls are actually working. The fourth calls for an independent committee of each company’s board of directors to review reports from internal teams and external auditors.Some of the measures are already being used by major AI companies or resemble previous commitments made by them.The voluntary nature of the accord has drawn scepticism from some experts. Robin Jia, an assistant professor of computer science at the University of Southern California, questioned whether enough faith should be placed in companies policing themselves, saying it was important to ensure the leading AI labs’ intentions were “well-aligned with the broader interest of the American public.”Alex Pascal, executive director of the Berkman Klein Center for Internet and Society, criticised what he described as the agreement’s broad and vague language, arguing that reducing AI risks would require stronger legal liability and regulation.Amodei, who has been among the more outspoken voices warning about the risks of rapid AI development, also struck a cautious note at the White House.“The technology has very real risks.”“And, you know, the mechanism, how we address those risks is still under discussion,” Amodei said.Trump pushes ‘super intelligence’The agreement was announced alongside a broader White House push to accelerate AI development. Trump has insisted that the US should not impose restrictions that could slow its progress against China.“I will never stifle the growth of a technology that will be bigger than the industrial revolution,” Trump said at the unveiling of America.gov, an AI chatbot designed to help Americans navigate government services. “We can't stifle it, and we're leading by a lot.”Trump also signed an executive order directing the executive branch to replace the term “artificial intelligence” with “super intelligence”, or “SI”, in official communications and policy documents.“The Order directs all departments and agencies to use the terms ‘Super Intelligence’ and ‘SI’ in official correspondence, public communications, policy documents, and non-statutory documents within the executive branch and to no longer acknowledge the terms ‘Artificial Intelligence’ or ‘AI’,” the order declared.You use AI every day. articles.title: S Korea demands apology from Pyongyang over landmine blast
articles.summary: Blasts in the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) injured three South Korean personnel earlier this month.
articles.body:
South Korea's military has demanded an apology from North Korea for landmine blasts along their shared border that wounded South Korean soldiers earlier this month.

Three South Korean personnel were injured by explosions in the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) - a buffer zone separating the two Koreas, on 21 September.

South Korea said on Tuesday that the blasts, which happened on South Korea's side of the DMZ, were "highly likely" from North Korean mines. It vowed to take "corresponding measures" for what it said was a violation of a decades-old armistice.

North Korea has denied responsibility for the blasts, calling Seoul's claims "groundless" and a "farce" to escalate tensions on the peninsula.

Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, accused South Korea of "cooking up" the claims for "political and military provocation".

Kim denied suggestions that North Korean had crossed the border to plant the mines, calling it "a deliberate and planned strained assertion to shift the responsibility for escalating tension" to North Korea.

Her statement, published in state media on Wednesday, also warned the South to be "prepared for paying price for the farce of their own making."

South Korea says the mines are believed to have been laid by Pyongyang to fortify its border. In a statement on Wednesday, it called for North Korea to apologise for the blast and put an immediate stop to such fortification activities along the border.

South Korean Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul previously said on Tuesday that the blasts were a "clear" violation of the 1953 armistice, which halted active combat in the Korean War.

That armistice resulted in the creation of the 4km-wide (2.5mi) DMZ, a buffer strip containing the Military Demarcation Line which marks the land border between the two Koreas.

In the decades since, sporadic clashes and mine explosions have broken out in the DMZ.

In 2015, two South Korean soldiers were maimed by landmines while patrolling the area. South Korea said the mines had been secretly planted by North Korean soldiers near a South Korean guard post - a claim that Pyongyang denied.

Kim referenced that 2015 incident in her statement on Wednesday, claiming South Korea had used that as a "pretext" to escalate tensions, and were doing the same thing now.

Ties between Pyongyang and Seoul have only deteriorated since 2015, raising the risk of friction when such incidents happen.

Christopher Green, a senior consultant with Crisis Group, tells the BBC that "The North Koreans have been wilfully attempting to harden the border [and] eliminate inter-Korean relations".

As a result, he adds, the two Koreas no longer have the "same low-level communication" that they shared in 2015.

"Accidental escalation on the Korean Peninsula is always just a few steps away, and it's fewer steps now than it was in 2015," he says.

The United Nations Command, which conducted the on-site investigations into the blasts with the South Korean military, said it would handle the violation of the 1953 armistice "through established Armistice mechanisms".

"UNC remains committed to maintaining and enforcing the Armistice Agreement and fulfilling its responsibilities to preserve stability and prevent escalation on the Korean Peninsula," it said.

articles.title: Restaurant named after Xi Jinping attacked by Chinese nationals
articles.summary: The owner said he chose the name because he wanted to run the "best Chinese restaurant" in South Korea.
articles.body:
A restaurant in South Korea named after Chinese leader Xi Jinping has been vandalised by a group of Chinese nationals who fled home right after the attack, police say.

Surveillance footage from the restaurant in Seongnam, a city south of Seoul, shows four masked men storming the premises in the early hours of 24 September, smashing furniture and spraying lacquer.

The restaurant's owner told local media he picked the name Xi Jinping because he "wanted it to be the best Chinese restaurant [in South Korea]". He added that "There was no political intent".

The restaurant has been running for eight years but only began getting demands for a name change over the past year, The Chosun Daily reported.

The owner said that in August last year, when news broke that Xi would be attending the Asia Pacific Economic Co-operation Summit in South Korea, he received dozens of phone calls relating to these demands. Some people even offered money, he said.

"People claiming to run businesses in China proposed large sums if we changed the name," he told The Chosun Daily. "They were persistent."

In April this year, someone filed a complaint with South Korea's Ministry of Intellectual Property regarding a dish on the restaurant's menu called Xi Jinping Special Rice, but the ministry eventually closed the case, finding no issues.

The owner said last week's attack was the largest one he's experienced over the past year, telling local media the property damage amounted to about 15 million won ($11,100; £8,400).

Xi Jinping restaurant closed for five days following the attack and reopened on Tuesday. The owner says his team is now considering a new name for the eatery.

Police on Tuesday said the four suspects were Chinese men between the ages of 20 and 40. After the attack they are believed to have fled to Shanghai and Yantai, a city in China's Shandong province.

Police say they are planning to request red notices from Interpol for the four men. These are not arrest warrants, but rather requests to police around the world to detain someone pending extradition.

Xi Jinping restaurant serves a wide range of Chinese dishes, although its menu also includes some South Korean offerings, according to screenshots shared online. Google reviewers have given it an average score of four out of five stars.

articles.title: They built 40 life-size bison from steel, plywood and burlap in Brooklyn, then made the giant herd walk through New York City
articles.summary: For two days in September 2026, a herd of 40 life-size bison walked through New York City. The animals were puppets, hand-built at St.
articles.body: For two days in September 2026, a herd of 40 life-size bison walked through New York City. The animals were puppets, hand-built at St. Ann’s Warehouse in Brooklyn using steel, plywood, burlap and paper, and they moved through Lower Manhattan on Sept. 18 and Downtown Brooklyn on Sept. 19. The free public event, Return of the Buffalo: Tatanka Owe Akupi, was presented by St. Ann’s Warehouse, The Walk Productions and KBH Arts and created by Amir Nizar Zuabi in partnership with Elders from the Lenape and Lakota tribes. Each bison was operated by three puppeteers, while more than 100 volunteer puppeteers from around the world were trained to reproduce the animals’ movements. The event combined the giant puppets with music, poetry, ceremonies, dance and other performances at locations across the city.How 40 life-size bison puppets were made from steel, plywood and burlapThe puppets were designed by Ukwanda Puppets, a collective from Cape Town, South Africa, and locally fabricated and assembled at St. Ann’s Warehouse in Brooklyn. The team had experience creating large-scale puppetry, including work on War Horse. For this project, Ukwanda created a prototype in Cape Town before digitising the plans for laser cutting, welding and fabrication. The finished bison were about six feet tall and nine to 10 feet long, with each puppet weighing more than 80 pounds. The head alone weighed more than 40 pounds. The puppets were made from steel, plywood, burlap and paper, with recycled and recyclable materials used in their construction.Three puppeteers operated each bison. One worked at the rear and controlled the back legs, another worked at the front to move the head, and a third performer stayed outside to support the head and relay information to the puppeteers inside, who had limited visibility. The performers spent days learning how to make the bison walk, breathe and move together as a herd. Some of the commands used during training, including instructions such as “gallop,” “gentle stop”, and “regroup,” were given in Xhosa and Arabic, languages connected to members of the production team. The production's puppetry director, Craig Leo, said the experience of moving through New York as part of an entire herd was a rare opportunity for the volunteer performers. The project also involved a substantial volunteer-training effort. In coverage of the finished puppets, amNewYork reported that more than 100 volunteer puppeteers from around the world had been trained.Return of the Buffalo route: From Bowling Green Park to Foley Square and Brooklyn Bridge ParkOn Friday, Sept. 18, the herd travelled through Lower Manhattan from Bowling Green Park to Foley Square between 5 and 7:30 p.m. On Saturday, Sept. 19, it moved through Downtown Brooklyn from Abolitionist Place to Brooklyn Bridge Park between 2 and 4:30 p.m. The procession was accompanied by a wide range of artists and performers. St. Ann’s official list included Sam Waterston, Susan Sarandon, Rosario Dawson, Laurie Anderson, Rhiannon Giddens, Nathalie Joachim and Talie Cerin, Davóne Tines & The Truth, Resistance Revival Chorus, Dither, Caridad De La Luz, Daphne Rubin-Vega, Cannupa Hanska Luger, Native Pride Dancers, Chaske Spencer, Pilobolus Dance Company, Fogo Azul marching band, Heather Christian and the Terce Choir, and Brooklyn United Marching Band.The herd stopped at locations of historical significance along the routes, with live music, readings, dance, ceremonies and other performances taking place around the bison. Coverage of the Manhattan procession also described a stop outside the New York Stock Exchange, where heavy-metal guitarists performed. The event was designed as a public spectacle that people could watch without buying a ticket. Instead of remaining inside a theatre, the performers and puppets moved through streets, parks and public spaces, bringing the production directly into the city.Why the buffalo story matters: From tens of millions to fewer than 1,000The spectacle was built around the dramatic history of the American bison. Bison once numbered in the tens of millions across North America, but their population fell to fewer than 1,000 by the late 19th century. Today, hundreds of thousands of bison are estimated to live in the United States. The production connects that history with the relationship between bison and Indigenous peoples. Return of the Buffalo was created in partnership with Elders from the Lenape and Lakota tribes, whose participation helped shape the production's treatment of Indigenous history, culture and the significance of the buffalo.The Lakota subtitle, Tatanka Owe Akupi, was used alongside the English title Return of the Buffalo. Rather than relying on differing English translations of the Lakota phrase, the production itself presents the two titles together. For the artists behind the project, the bison's near disappearance and recovery provided a way to explore themes of loss, renewal and the relationship between people, animals and land. St. Ann’s artistic director Susan Feldman described the buffalo's history as a story of both near extinction and a later effort to restore the species. Karen Brooks Hopkins, founder and producer of KBH Arts, described the production as “the largest public art spectacle in America.” That is the organiser's characterisation rather than an independently established record. The New York performances have now ended, but the project may not be finished. The Walk Productions says it is exploring future appearances for Return of the Buffalo, leaving open the possibility that the life-size herd could eventually walk through other cities.You use AI every day. articles.title: Move to rejoin EU among options for UK, says Andy Burnham
articles.summary: The prime minister tells the BBC the current Brexit settlement has caused "more harm than good".
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has suggested rejoining the EU is among options the government could examine to reshape the UK's long-term relationship with Europe.

The prime minister told the BBC the current Brexit settlement had caused "more harm than good" and he wanted to look at "what is doable" to repair relations.

It comes after he pledged in his Labour conference speech on Tuesday to explore closer ties with the bloc at a delayed summit later this year.

The move could set up a huge dividing line at the next general election, with the Conservatives accusing him of trying to "reopen old wounds by restarting the battles of the Brexit years".

Last week, Burnham left the door open to campaigning at the next general election for a mandate to rejoin the EU.

As a candidate in the Makerfield by-election that propelled his return to Parliament, he had promised not to "re-run" Brexit arguments and said he was "not proposing that the UK considers rejoining the EU".

But his latest comments are the clearest indication yet he could make a decisive break from Labour's 2024 election manifesto, which pledged to "make Brexit work" whilst ruling out rejoining either its customs union or single market.

Predecessor Sir Keir Starmer had instead tried to carve out a more limited reset in relations, including aligning with EU food standards, a youth visa deal and relinking British industry to the EU's carbon trading regime .

Sir Keir's departure from office delayed a summer summit with the EU until later this year, at which time Burnham has also said he wants to publish a 10-year plan to transform the UK economy.

Burnham pledges not to 're-run' Brexit arguments

Davey promises tax cuts for millions if UK rejoins EU single market

Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Burnham said he did not want to leave the question of the EU relationship "hanging" and he wanted to be clear on "where we want Britain to go in the next decade".

Asked whether he wanted the UK to rejoin the EU, he replied that he wanted to "look at the options".

He added he had previously advocated such a move within his lifetime, whilst acknowledging it was "not necessarily the case that that is now".

"We could stay as we are. That's definitely an option, if people think this is the right place to stay," he told the programme.

"We could look at what [former Chancellor] George Osborne has said about a customs union, we could look at what the Liberal Democrats said at their conference about the single market, or we could go all the way."

"So there are clearly options that need to be considered, and we have to look at what is doable and what would be the pros and cons of each," he added.

In his conference speech on Tuesday, Burnham blamed Brexit for a loss of control over both immigration and the economy, telling delegates he did not believe the current relationship was "good enough".

He told activists he wanted to use the rescheduled summit later this year to lay out "different options" for the UK's long-term relationship with Europe.

He promised to "find consensus" on an option to clarify the UK's position, although did not offer further detail of how this would be measured.

In response to Burnham's conference speech, Conservative deputy leader Alex Burghart said: "Labour cannot pin the blame for their disastrous economic decisions on a vote that happened over a decade ago.

"Besides, they are already dragging us into the European Union via the back door with their EU reset."

articles.title: Dead animals found in Brentford canal amid water quality concerns
articles.summary: Residents in Brentford raise concerns about sewage flowing into the local canal network.
articles.body:
Residents in Brentford have raised concerns about sewage flowing into the local canal network, with dead animals washing up over the summer.

Paul Keane, general manager of watersports charity Brentford Community Boathouse, told the Brentford and Syon Area Forum that the problem had been worsened by the "epidemic of heat" this summer.

The animals were mostly found in the Brentford Lock basin, where the Grand Union Canal meets the River Thames.

"We saw dead foxes, dead ducks and there was a dead cat," Keane told BBC London.

"Because of the stagnant water and the fact that the water wasn't travelling anywhere, we were going past them every day in exactly the same spot."

Brentford Community Boathouse events officer Kelly Everden, who volunteered on a clean-up operation organised by Keane, said the children who used the canal were worst affected.

"It's really upsetting on behalf of the children, because that's not anything that they should ever be faced with, especially with a pet cat," she said.

Keane said the problem was at least partly down to misconnections, where plumbing from housing developments is wrongly linked to surface water drains rather than sewers, sending untreated waste into waterways.

"The big fly in the ointment is sewage coming into the canal," he said.

"That gets worse in the summer when the water is moving slowly, and some of that is historic, but also a contemporary misdirecting of sewage into storm drains."

He said he did not believe this was Hounslow Council's fault, but that it needed attention "if we do want to develop usage of the canal, particularly for children on the water".

He added: "The water has to be hygienic, and there are times when it simply isn't. It's a very difficult issue, but it needs an overall strategy."

Keane said the animals were predominantly found with E. coli and botulism, and that the most stagnant stretch was within the locks around Boston Manor Park.

Warm, still water holds less oxygen, creating the conditions in which botulism thrives and speeding up the growth of E. coli.

Hounslow councillor Katherine Dunne said officers in Ealing and Brent were examining misconnections through a River Brent catchment group, and committee chair councillor Dan Bowring urged residents to contact their ward councillors.

"All councillors in Brentford will be concerned about this," he said.

The Canal and River Trust said it aimed to remove any dead animal as quickly as possible. Aquatic weed has been a particular problem at Brentford, it said, because both of its west London weed clearance boats were out of action at the same time.

Thames Water said the area was known to have issues with misconnections and that, while it was not responsible for third-party drainage, it was working with property owners and councils.

The Environment Agency said the area remained in drought, which can affect river health, and that it would continue investigating reports of pollution.
